title: R-coverage/DuckDB-call hybrid: completed scoped qualification
status: PASS; research qualification complete; production not adopted
decision: Worthwhile moderate integration candidate if the user chooses the measured historical benefit over additional maintenance; adoption requires a separate user decision.

selected_sources.implementation: R plus handwritten SQL through DBI/DuckDB; no custom C++/Rcpp. Python/shell are qualification controls. Coverage/scientific calculations unchanged.
selected_sources.maintenance: Native factor/type/name/list restoration, ordering and NA semantics, DBI/DuckDB behavior, and private database ownership/failure/cleanup handling.

schema_and_fix.valid_input_gap: Native empty producer SBS/indel call tables retain zero-level factors; the frozen helper rejected them. Original empty fixtures retained existing levels and missed the gap.
changes: Use SQL VARCHAR with retained R factor prototypes when levels are empty.
Follow native vctrs factor-name casting and current common prototypes.
Default omitted auxiliary names to blank while retaining explicit NA names.
schema_and_fix.scope: Producer-schema audit follows the current successful pipeline paths. Named-factor fixtures extend the supported contract; audited producer factor columns are unnamed. Zero-level factors are valid producer output. This is not a general R serializer or proof of all barcode/MDB configurations.

contracts.method: R identical(), including types/classes/attributes/order; no normalization or tolerance. Includes empty factors, name/list/NA semantics, SQL selection/counts, overflow guards and cleanup.

mitochondrial.baseline: All three native controls passed. Frozen hybrid failed zero_mt_reads and mt_reads_zero_raw_calls; mt_raw_calls_filtered_zero passed. Failed artifacts retained.
mitochondrial.scope: Complete burdens against retained native controls, with existing fixtures/configuration; no extraction/filter rerun. These small fixtures are correctness proofs, not performance claims.

real_call_replay.method: Strict whole ordinary-object and component identity against independent native bind_rows/project/count/filter oracle, including attributes, factor/name/list/NA semantics and order. Successful owned cleanup in all four workers.
real_call_replay.scope: Call storage only; no coverage/BED or complete burden replay. Actual factor levels agree across selected chunks; synthetic transitions are in the separate contracts.

call_store_performance.method: Two fresh workers per arm, old/fixed/fixed/old. Actual CPU is Linux RUSAGE_CHILDREN user+system for waited descendants; RSS is largest waited process high-water memory, not cgroup/job aggregate.
call_store_performance.included: Package startup, full input QS loading, selection, append, projection/count/restoration, checkpoint/close, ordinary QS save and private cleanup. Both arms additionally restore the complete raw-final table for proof.
call_store_performance.interpretation: No appreciable regression at this measured scale. Small differences are not a new speedup claim. Warmed caches, allocator/order effects and setup-dominated RSS remain; two repetitions per arm do not estimate small differences precisely.

excluded_failed_preflight.cause: Python preflight assumed a named JSON numeric object, but jsonlite emitted an array. Python-only correction; scientific sources/inputs unchanged. Not a science or performance failure.

limits.rows: The per-table 2^31-1 integer row cap and integer count output remain. Safe zero-column constructors confirm that the pinned native tibble/vctrs path rejects larger ordinary tables. Synthetic counters exercise the last two IDs and guarded overflow without allocating billions of rows; no cardinality benchmark or general long-vector claim.
limits.memory: Memory is not bounded independently of input size: R coverage, collected call tables and final ordinary QS assembly remain materialized.
limits.scope: Identified schema and three mitochondrial edge checks are closed for the selected helper and pinned package context. No blanket all-input/all-configuration claim.
limits.not_repeated: No corrected-helper full60 timing/scientific replay, new downstream 310-export replay, or latest full-Nextflow run.
limits.production: Hybrid remains outside production, pending a separate user adoption decision. One ordinary public QS2 is preserved.

historical_evidence.interpretation: Full15/full60 metrics and complete full60/downstream exactness proofs belong to the frozen pre-qualification helper. Full60 observed 15.72% actual CPU and 15.04% process-peak reduction; mixed preparation and shared-cache/timing caveats remain. These are not corrected-helper or whole-pipeline savings. The separate full-SQL coverage rejection is unchanged.
